Mr. Deepak Bisht, learned Deputy
Advocate General for the State of
Uttarakhand.
2. The present bail application has
been moved by the applicant, who is in
judicial custody in connection with
FIR/Case Crime No. 39 of 2025,
registered at Police Station Devprayag,
District Tehri Garhwal, for the offences
punishable under Section 29 read with
Sections 8/20/27/60 of the Narcotic
Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act,
1985 (hereinafter referred to as the
"NDPS Act").
3. Heard learned counsel for the
applicant and learned State Counsel and
perused the material available on record.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant
submits that the applicant has been
implicated in the present case under
Section 29 of the NDPS Act solely on the
basis of the disclosure statement made
by the co-accused, who was
apprehended at the spot. It is further
submitted that the applicant has no
concern with the alleged recovery and
has no criminal antecedents. Learned
counsel further submits that the co-accused, who was apprehended at the
spot, has already been enlarged on bail
and, therefore, the applicant is also
entitled to bail on the ground of parity.

5. Per contra, learned State Counsel
has opposed the prayer for bail; however,
he fairly acknowledges that the applicant
has raised a plea of parity with the co-accused, who has already been granted
bail.
6. Having considered the submissions
advanced by learned counsel for the
parties and upon perusal of the material
available on record, this Court finds that
the applicant has been implicated
primarily on the basis of the disclosure
statement of the co-accused. It is also
relevant to note that the co-accused,
who was apprehended at the spot, has
already been enlarged on bail. Further,
no criminal antecedents have been
attributed to the applicant. Having
regard to the overall facts and
circumstances of the case, particularly
the nature of the allegations and the
principle of parity, this Court is of the
considered view that the applicant has
made out a case for grant of bail.
7. Accordingly, without expressing
any opinion on the merits of the case or
the ultimate outcome of the trial, this
Court is inclined to enlarge the applicant
on bail.
8. The bail application is, accordingly,
allowed.
9. Let the applicant be released on
bail upon executing a personal bond and
furnishing two reliable sureties, each in
the like amount, to the satisfaction of
the Court concerned, subject to the
following conditions:
(i) The applicant shall regularly attend
the proceedings before the trial court
and shall not seek any unnecessary
adjournment.
(ii) The applicant shall not, directly or
indirectly, make any inducement, threat
or promise to any person acquainted
with the facts of the case so as to

dissuade such person from disclosing
such facts to the Court or to any police
officer.
(iii) The applicant shall not leave India
without prior permission of the trial
court.
10. It is clarified that, in the event of
misuse of the liberty of bail or violation
of any of the conditions imposed
hereinabove, the complainant/informant
shall be at liberty to move an appropriate
application before the competent court
seeking cancellation of the applicant's
bail.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
